subject: Order Form — payee split, invoice routing & tax allocation
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-analytics.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwoood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme-analytics.com
Date: Wed, 4 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form questions — invoice payee split and tax allocation

Hi Marissa / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Procurement ran the draft Order Form past our tax and treasury teams and a couple items need clarification before we can issue a PO:

1) Payee / invoice split: our EU entity (Acme Analytics Ltd) needs to be invoiced for EU spend and the US entity (Acme Analytics Inc) for US spend. Can Redwood issue split invoices (two invoices per invoice event) or do you require two separate Order Forms / billing entities?

2) Tax handling: for EU invoices we need a VAT-reverse-charge note and Acme's VAT ID on the invoice; for US invoices we need the standard sales tax treatment. Who on your side confirms the taxonomy?

3) Net terms request: treasury is pushing net45 for the consolidated deal but would accept net30 on the US invoices only. Is that feasible, or do you need a uniform net term across the account?

4) Minimum commit allocation: can the minimum commit be apportioned by entity so that usage against the US entity counts toward its portion and EU usage toward the EU portion?

I've attached the PO template the team will sign once we confirm paths. If easier, we can do a short call with legal/finance tomorrow.

Appreciate a quick reply — our procurement window closes next Friday.

Best,
Liam
Director, Procurement
Acme Analytics

Attachment: Acme_PO_20250603.pdf (application/pdf)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 4 Jun 2025 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form questions — invoice payee split and tax allocation

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Kimberly (billing & tax) and Karthik (legal/contract) so we can align quickly. Summary of what we need to confirm on our side and proposed approach: 

- Payee split: we can support split invoicing without separate Order Forms but will need to map each subscription line to a billing entity in our system. That requires the legal entity names, addresses and tax IDs for both Acme entities.

- VAT language: Kimberly can add the reverse-charge annotation for EU invoices; please confirm Acme Analytics Ltd's VAT ID and whether you expect us to gross-up or leave amounts net of VAT.

- Net terms: we generally have a single net term per billing entity. If you want net30 on US invoices and net45 on EU invoices, we can do that only if each invoice is issued under the corresponding Redwood billing entity mapped to the Acme entity.

- Minimum commit: we can apportion the commitment across entities in the Order Form (e.g., $300k for US / $200k for EU) and track consumption separately. That will feed billing and reporting so usage counts toward the relevant tranche.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Karthik to review Order Form redlines (I attached orderform_v3_redlines.pdf) and confirm any legal flags.
2) Kimberly to confirm invoice annotation language and the gross-up operating model.
3) If all good, we’ll prepare a single Order Form with a billing-entity mapping appendix and two invoice templates (EU / US).

Available for a 30-min call tomorrow between 9–11am PT if you want to run through live.

Thanks — will follow up after Karthik and Kimberly chime in.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Office: +1 415 555 0123
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-analytics.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 4 Jun 2025 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form questions — invoice payee split and tax allocation

Thanks Marissa — quick legal view from my side after reviewing the attached redlines (orderform_v3_redlines.pdf):

- Single Order Form with a billing-entity appendix is preferable (keeps commercial terms centralized). We will include an appendix that lists Acme Analytics Inc (US) and Acme Analytics Ltd (EU) with mapping to Redwood billing entities.

- Net terms: we can support per-entity net terms provided the appendix is explicit and the invoicing system issues separate invoices per billing entity. Legal wants a short clause stating that failure to pay on one entity will not (by itself) be treated as a breach by the other — unless you want cross-guarantee language.

- Minimum commit apportionment is OK. We should add a table in the Order Form specifying commit allocation and an aggregation rule for usage overage (i.e., whether overages on one entity apply to the global commitment or are charged locally). My preference is to keep overage charged at the local entity rate unless you approve global pooling.

- Tax indemnity: we will not assume tax liability; the Order Form should state that Acme is responsible for providing tax IDs and evidence (VAT exemption certificates or equivalent).

Action items for Redwood:
- Marissa: confirm whether Acme wants global pooling for overage credits or strict per-entity accounting.
- Kimberly: provide the exact invoice annotation language and example invoice templates so we can confirm doc language.
- Ben: FYI on commercial/discounting impact if the commit is split — might need to confirm pricing bands.

Happy to jump on the call if needed — I can be available at 10am PT tomorrow.

- Karthik
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-analytics.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 5 Jun 2025 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form questions — invoice payee split and tax allocation

Liam — thanks, we appreciate the quick turnaround. Couple of confirmations from our side after internal sync: 

1) We will produce a single Order Form with a billing-entity appendix and two invoice templates (EU / US). Please send the legal names, addresses and tax IDs for both entities by end of day Friday so Kimberly can populate templates.

2) Net terms: Redwood will support net30 for US invoices and net45 for EU invoices as requested, tied to billing-entity issuance. That means you will receive two invoices for each billing event (if there is cross-entity usage, see #4).

3) Minimum commit: we will apportion the minimum commit in the Order Form (example below). Overages will be charged to the entity that incurred them; we can discuss a global pooling model but pricing tiers / discounts will change if we pool.

   Example allocation (for the proposed $500k commitment):
   - Acme Analytics Inc (US) — $300,000
   - Acme Analytics Ltd (EU) — $200,000

4) Cross-entity usage: if you want usage from one entity to count against the other's commitment we can add a global pooling clause; Ben, can you confirm whether pricing bands should be preserved per-entity or blended? If Acme prefers simplicity now, we recommend per-entity accounting and revisit pooling in renewal.

5) Next steps: Liam to return entity legal details + confirm whether Acme wants global pooling. Kimberly will send invoice template language by EOD Friday; Karthik will turn the appendix into contract language and share a redline. I will consolidate and post the updated Order Form to DocuSign for signature.

Call option: 10am PT tomorrow if Acme wants to run through the appendix live.

Thanks all — looking forward to closing this week.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
